items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to enacting the broadcast employees' freedom to work act; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5616

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the labor law, in relation to enacting the broadcast employees'
freedom to work act; and to repeal certain provisions of such law
relating thereto

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To clarify the protections of persons employed in the broadcast
industry.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section 1 provides that this act shall be known and may be cited as
the "broadcast employees' freedom to work act".

Section 2 repeals section 202-k of the Labor Law and adds a new
section 202-k. This new section clarifies the definitions of
"broadcasting industry employer" and "broadcast employee" while
adding the clarifying definitions of the following terms and phrases:
"covered broadcasting services", "management employee", "require as a
condition of employment", and "covenant not to compete". Under this
section, an entity considered to provide covered broadcasting
services must have at least 30 percent of its assets or employees
dedicated primarily to such services. This section also clarifies
that covenants not to compete applicable during the course of
employment are not prohibited. Section one also provides exclusions
to prohibited covenants not to compete including (a) enforcement
during the remaining term of employment as set forth in the
employment agreement, in the event of employment termination; (b)
enforcement of a covenant agreed to by a broadcast employee in return
for additional and independent consideration; (c) enforcement of an
exclusive good-faith negotiation provision; (d) enforcement of a
right of first refusal; (e) enforcement of any post contractual
restriction for a broadcast employee earning more than one hundred thou
sand dollars annually; or (f) the enforcement by a broadcasting
industry employer of any post-contractual confidentiality or
non-disclosure provision. Finally, the section prohibits the waiver
of any protection
provided by the new section 202-k.

EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW WHICH THIS BILL WOULD ALTER:
Section 202-k of the Labor Law prohibits as a condition of employment,
whether in an employment contract or otherwise, that a broadcast
employee or prospective broadcast employee refrain from obtaining
employment (a) in any specified geographic area; (b) for a specific
period of time;
or (c) with a particular employer or in any particular industry after
the conclusion of employment. This section also provides civil
liability for violations of these protections.

JUSTIFICATION:
Section 202-k of the Labor Law was intended to protect broadcast
employees by prohibiting, as a condition of employment, covenants not
to compete. The protections provided by this section are, however,
overly broad and unintentionally capture a number of items and


situations including, among others, post-contractual confidentiality
or non-disclosure provisions and accepting non-compete convenants in
return for additional independent consideration. The bill provides
these exceptions and thus offers additional freedom and flexibility
for broadcast employees and reasonable protections for broadcast
employers relating to potentially sensitive confidential information
respectively.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
S.5890

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Enacts the broadcast employees' freedom to work act.
